newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares mixed, big banks gain.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares mixed, big banks gain.

text.p: Lithuanian shares were mixed on Wednesday with the big banks gaining while other blue chips lost ground, dealers said.
Overall central market volume was just over 1.25 million litas and the Litin A index edged up by 36.44 points to 2,560.23. Block trades turned over around 156,000 litas.
"We anticipated a turbulent week...all of the big shareholders' meetings are over now and of course the response by investors has varied," said one dealer.
Dealers said that some investors were bailing now with dividends in hand while others were snapping up shares in anticipation of further gains.
The country's biggest private banks, Vilniaus and Hermis, advanced.
Vilniaus rose to 227.70 litas from 207.00 litas in light trade of 3,643 litas while Hermis Bank jumped 4.21 percent to 198.00 litas in trade of 123,750 litas.

Both banks reported huge profits for 1996 but the market's response has been mixed. Vilniaus Bank paid out only a fraction of its earnings in dividends and dealers said some buyers were put off by this move.
But dealers said other investors regard it and Hermis as good buys at the moment and are impressed by the apparent recovery of the banking sector, which was thrown into crisis late in 1995.
Siauliai Bank also gained, rising to 85.80 litas from 78.00 litas in trade of almost 4,300 litas.
Other blue chips fell, including Birzai Dairy, which dropped ten percent to 8.73 litas in trade worth almost 14,000 litas.
The Lithuanian Sea Shipping Company also slipped to 8.51 litas from 8.60 litas in trade of over 146,000 litas.
